en: Theragāthā 2.16 Dukanipāta, Second Chapter The Elder Cūḷa-Panthaka I am one who has crossed over the flood, One who has reached the further shore; I have transcended all attachments, And am now free from all bonds. I have abandoned all sensual pleasures, And have cut off the stream of craving; Having severed the net of existence, I dwell in peace, unshakable. I am not subject to birth again, My mind is well-liberated; Having attained the destruction of taints, I have realized the state of an arahant. I have no more rebirths for me, My burden is laid down; Having lived the holy life, I have done what was to be done. I have no more afflictions, My mind is well-concentrated; Having attained the destruction of taints, I have realized the state of an arahant. The Verses of the Elder Mahākāḷa:
“A large, dark woman with the form of a crane,
having broken one thigh bone and then another;”
Having pierced one arm and then the other,
and having pierced her head like a bowl of curd,
she sits here, having joined them together.
The fool who, being ignorant, creates acquisitions,
therefore, one who understands should not create acquisitions.
"May I not lie again with a broken head," said the Elder Mahākāḷa.
